{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "The seventh letter did not come. Ines waited for it the way you wait for a step on the stair that has always come at the same hour, and when the hour passed she felt the absence more sharply than she had felt any of the arrivals.

She told herself it was nothing. Letters stop. People stop writing them. That was the ordinary end of things and she had seen it before, in other tins, in other years.

But the pipes had changed. She noticed that on the Thursday, standing in the courtyard with the bucket she had not meant to bring. The low even sound had broken into something uneven, a catch and a rush, a catch and a rush, like breath that was trying not to be heard. She set the bucket down. She did not fill it.

That night she took the six letters out and laid them in a row on the counter and read them in order, which she had never done. Read that way they were not six letters. They were one, cut into pieces, and the pieces leaned toward something. The water. The quiet upstairs. The thanks. The key.

She went through the drawers behind the register. Ribbon, string, the good scissors, a button jar. At the very back of the lowest drawer, under a folded paper pattern, her fingers found something small and cold and iron.

She did not remember putting it there. She was almost certain she had not.

Upstairs, very faintly, the pipes caught and rushed, caught and rushed, and then, for the first time in weeks, fell silent."}
